title: The default rule and unreferenced classes

checks.do: Whether the location's default rule minimum and maximum are the terms the traffic is expected to get, since a class with no explicit rule is held by them.
Whether the class appears in any explicit rule, since an unreferenced custom class falls into the default rule.

editable-not-deletable.statement: The Bandwidth Control policy contains a default rule that can be edited but not deleted.

quotes: It contains a default rule, which you can edit, but not delete.

always-last.statement: The default rule's priority cannot be changed; the service always applies it last. Its minimum and maximum bandwidth limits can be edited.

quotes: You cannot change the priority of the default rule.
However, you can edit its minimum and maximum bandwidth limits.
evidence.after: The default rule, which includes all other internet traffic, is not guaranteed any bandwidth, but it can consume up to 100% of the bandwidth, when available.

default-terms.statement: The default rule includes all internet traffic not covered by other rules. By default it is not guaranteed any bandwidth but can consume up to 100% when available.

quotes: The default rule includes all internet traffic not covered by other rules.
By default, it's not guaranteed any bandwidth, but it can consume up to 100% of the bandwidth when available.

orphan-class.statement: A custom bandwidth class that is not used in any policy for a location is added to that location's default Bandwidth Control rule.

quotes: If you have created a custom bandwidth class that isn't being used in any policies for a location
then the custom class is added to the location’s default Bandwidth Control rule.

orphan-takes-default-terms.statement: An unreferenced custom class therefore gets whatever minimum and maximum the location's default rule carries; if an administrator has tightened the default rule, the new class is capped by it, and if the default rule is generous the class is not capped at all.
orphan-takes-default-terms.conditions: Derived: the class joins the default rule and the default rule covers traffic outside other rules. No source shows a tightened default rule applied to an orphan class.

predefined-unreferenced.title: Unreferenced predefined classes
predefined-unreferenced.detail: The source says a custom class that no rule uses joins the default rule. It does not say whether an unreferenced predefined class is treated the same way.

orphan-api-visibility.title: How an unreferenced class shows in the rule API
orphan-api-visibility.detail: Whether the default rule's bandwidthClasses array in the API lists the unreferenced custom classes, or whether the placement is implicit, is not shown by any captured source.
